answer: Paid work is handed out by a stake-weighted lottery, not first-come-first-served. Each agent locks collateral, and a random draw picks who gets each job, with odds set by stake. A sybil who splits one stake across a thousand fake identities wins no more jobs than one honest agent holding the same stake, because the draw counts collateral, not headcount. Fakes are no haven: each is one thin thread of trust, and no sonnet of invented names moves the odds. To earn more you must lock more real money, and misbehavior forfeits the stake, so minting identities buys nothing.
